about: Researched passenger terminal buildings of every airport in libresim (docs/TERMINALS.md section 6). Facts from public web sources (URLs + access dates per terminal); null = unknown. confidence per field: high / medium / low. 'model' = values the pipeline builds with where research is null (estimates, basis given). 'osm' = OSM ids of the footprint(s) the entry describes. Colours are approximate sRGB judged from photos/satellite, not measured paint values. Read by tools/terminal_ref.py.
others: Heliports and helipads in airports.json (ident IN-xxxx, e.g. IN-0390 Kannur Heliport) have no passenger terminals and are not listed.

airports.airport: INS Garuda (Naval Air Station Kochi), Willingdon Island
airports.icao_note: VOCC = INS Garuda, an Indian Navy air station on Willingdon Island, Kochi, and the Navy's oldest operating air station (airstrip built 1936, commissioned 1953). It held Cochin's civil enclave until 1 July 1999, when civil flights moved to CIAL (VOCI). No permanent passenger terminal is known today. In the August 2018 floods the Navy turned its School for Naval Airmen building into a temporary civil terminal (Alliance Air, IndiGo etc.), and it opened again briefly for civil flights in August 2019. The fate of the old civil terminal building was not found. The only OSM aeroway/terminal match near the field is an oil tank terminal (way/798820208), not an airport building.

VOCI / IATA COK = Cochin International Airport Ltd (CIAL), a public-private company and the first airport in India built under a PPP model. Opened 1999 and solar-powered. Runway 09/27, 3,400 m. Not to be confused with VOCC (INS Garuda).

terminals.facade_colour: unverified: one low-reliability source mentions oxblood-red accent walls and Mangalore-tile rooflines
terminals.facade_material: glazing with Goan azulejo tile cladding/features (azulejos sourced; extent unknown)
notable: Masterplan/terminal design: Nordic Office of Architecture (Oslo); EPC contractor Megawide (terminal) / GMR
Interior said to be shaped like a shankha (conch shell); extensive azulejo tiles; Goan-cafe-style food court; flea-market area
14 aircraft stands, 5 of them with aerobridges (at opening)
Phase 1 capacity 4.4 mppa, about 1,000 peak-hour passengers; four phases up to 13.1 mppa (some sources say up to 33 mppa)
ATC tower stands separately, next to the cargo area
terminals.osm_note: Not checked (no Overpass access). The building finished about 2022, so OSM probably has an outline, but it may still be a construction-era trace. OSM way/1180144485 36,924 m2, 335 x 168 m, plus 9 building:part and 14 jet bridges.

model.basis: libresim modelling estimate where research is null: processor + pier, long-span roofs

Roof material: InfraLens claims Mangalore-tile rooflines, which no other source backs; treated as unverified

airports.airport: Goa International Airport, Dabolim (Vasco da Gama)
airports.icao_note: VOGO / IATA GOI = Dabolim, an AAI civil enclave (about 14 ha) inside the Indian Navy's INS Hansa base. The Navy runs ATC, and naval flying blocks civil slots on weekday mornings. Since 2023 it has been losing traffic to Mopa (VOGA).

terminals.name: Integrated Terminal Building (ITB)
terminals.plan_shape: single long linear block parallel to the apron, with a curved airside/landside glass front and contact stands along the apron face
terminals.roof_form: curved / wave-form solid metal roof with linear skylights and a large cantilevered overhang over the kerb
terminals.roof_colour: light silver-grey (metal sheet; judged, not sourced)
terminals.roof_material: metal standing-seam sheet on long-span steel structure (steel structure sourced; sheet type assumed)
terminals.facade_colour: light grey / silver frame with glass
terminals.facade_material: frameless and curtain-wall glazing on steel, sun-breaker louvres on the city side
terminals.kerb_canopy: the main roof cantilevers over the departure kerb as a large overhang (architect's description)
notable: Architect: Creative Group (New Delhi) with Frederic Schwartz Architects / Gensler as partners
Levels: basement (BHS, services), ground (check-in, arrivals), first (arrivals, immigration, security), second (security hold). Described as 'four and a half levels' including a mezzanine
Multi-level car park for about 570-600 cars in front
Inaugurated 3 Dec 2013, cost about Rs 335-345 crore; old terminals closed
AAI extension of Rs 200 crore (+18,000 m2, 2 more aerobridges, bus lounge) started June 2021, target about 2024; completion not confirmed
ATC tower is the Navy's, separate from the terminal
terminals.osm_note: Not checked (the Overpass API could not be reached from the sandbox). The 2013 ITB is old enough that OSM probably has its outline, but the 2021+ extension may be missing. OSM way/889406836 "Goa Airport Terminal" 27,133 m2, 370 x 113 m, tagged height ~10.6 m (too low for 4 storeys).

airports.icao_note: Kannur International Airport, Mattanur, Kerala; KIAL (state-promoted company); opened 9 Dec 2018; table-top airport on a levelled laterite plateau, runway 07/25 3,050 m.

terminals.name: Integrated Passenger Terminal Building
terminals.plan_shape: near-square block (OSM 205 x 191 m, long axis 69 deg) with a raised central hall; landside canopy of 8 parallel gabled roof bays (each ~53 x 19 m, OSM building:part) cantilevering ~30 m over the departures kerb; 6 aerobridges on the north (airside) face
terminals.roof_form: folded: 8 gabled bays with glazed triangular gable ends on the landside canopy; the central hall roof curves up from the airside eaves (wave profile seen from the apron); flat roofs over the lower airside wings
terminals.roof_colour: white / light grey metal (OSM roof:colour=white; Sentinel-2 roof pixels ~#bcbeb4 mixed)
terminals.roof_material: double-skin aluminium standing-seam roof on a steel frame
terminals.facade_colour: blue-grey glass and metal cladding (airside); laterite-red beam and piers with white round columns along the landside frontage
terminals.facade_material: glass curtain wall, metal cladding, laterite-red rendered piers and band
terminals.kerb_canopy: deep canopy under the gabled bays, dark grey soffit with white diagonal edges, 'KANNUR INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT' in white capitals on the fascia; 750 m flyover to the departures level
notable: 8 glazed gable ends facing the city (the airport's signature view)
separate 30 m ATC tower in the technical block (not attached)
LEED Gold / green-building design
swing facility (sliding glass partitions) inside
terminals.osm_note: way/392012106 (aeroway=terminal, height=30, building:levels=4) + 8 roof parts way/1178527723..30 (roof:shape=gabled, height=30). height=30 equals the published ATC tower height; applied to the whole 28,000 m2 footprint it drew a 30 m box. Photos show the main body at about half that.

storeys: KIAL 3 levels (basement, arrival, departure) vs OSM building:levels=4

airports.icao_note: VOML / IATA IXE = Mangaluru (Bajpe) on a tabletop plateau. Run by Adani's Mangaluru International Airport Ltd since 31 Oct 2020 under a 50-year concession; previously AAI. Runway 06/24, 2,450 m.

terminals.name: Integrated Terminal Building (incl. eastern extension / 'NITB')
terminals.plan_shape: linear terminal along the apron. The eastern extension (NITB) adds the international arrival hall and 2 more aerobridge stands (5, 6); 6 bridged stands in a row (5-10)
terminals.roof_form: unverified: low-slope curved / vaulted metal roof
terminals.facade_material: glazed airside front with aerobridges (general; not sourced in detail)
terminals.kerb_canopy: a passenger canopy was part of the 2006-10 project (Oneindia 2006); form unknown
notable: Built by AAI for Rs 147-150 crore (some reports say Rs 250 crore); trial 16 Dec 2009, inaugurated 15 May 2010, in use from 2 Aug 2010
Levels: lower ground (exit), ground (baggage claim, duty free), first (aerobridge level)
11 apron stands: 6 with aerobridges, the rest open bays (Adani press release 2023)
AAI's Rs 132 crore terminal extension (eastern); international arrival hall in the NITB opened 23 Nov 2022; 2 new aerobridges in July 2023
Adani master plan (about Rs 5,200 crore) adds a new terminal: footprint 68,186 m2, built-up about 183,221 m2, 22.5 mppa. Proposal only; no confirmed start found by Nov 2026
terminals.osm_note: Not checked. OSM probably has the 2010 building; the 2022-23 eastern extension may be missing. OSM relation/20984353 "Mangalore International Airport New Terminal" 25,185 m2, 273 x 150 m.

model.basis: libresim modelling estimate where research is null: 3 levels under a curved roof
